decisions.reason: Section H.1 says Anthropic may require prepayment in credits or offer credits, subject to Supplemental Credits Terms (line 39). These are credit and payment arrangements, not an allowed activity involving an allowed artifact; representing them as Use of an OriginalArtifact would be a placeholder.

Section H.1 permits Anthropic to update published rates, effective at the earlier of 30 days after posting or Customer otherwise receiving Notice (line 39). Rate-setting is not an allowed activity involving an allowed artifact, so Use of an OriginalArtifact is not a faithful representation.

Section H.3 says failure to pay amounts owed when due may result in suspension or termination of Customer’s access (line 41). The current rule seg-829805e920cff0551c647902 addresses Customer’s prohibition on access during suspension or after termination (lines 50–52), not Anthropic’s conditional discretion to suspend or terminate access for nonpayment. The candidate faithfully captures that distinct permission.

Section H.3 reserves other collection rights Anthropic may have (line 41), but does not specify what those rights are. The candidate’s Use of an OriginalArtifact does not express a concrete allowed activity or duty, and the unspecified rights cannot be extracted from the supplied text.

Section I.2.a is a right to terminate the Terms for convenience by Notice, with 30 days’ prior Notice required only when Anthropic terminates (line 46). The existing rule covers the same termination-right terms (lines 46–48). Terminating a contract is not permission to use a service; the candidate’s Use action is therefore not a service-use clause to add.

Section I.2.b permits either party to terminate for the other party’s material breach after 30 days’ prior Notice detailing the breach, unless cured within that period (line 47). The existing rule covers this termination right and its conditions (lines 46–48). The candidate’s Use action misrepresents a contract-termination procedure as service use.

Section I.2.c permits Anthropic to terminate the Terms immediately with Notice if it reasonably believes or determines that providing Services to Customer is prohibited by applicable law (line 48). The existing rule includes this termination right (lines 46–48). This permission concerns termination of the Terms, not permission to use a service; the candidate’s Use action is inapposite.

Section I.3.a permits Anthropic to suspend access to any portion or all of the Services on the listed alternative grounds (line 50). The existing rule seg-829805e920cff0551c647902 addresses Customer’s resulting restriction on access while suspended, not Anthropic’s distinct conditional permission to suspend access (lines 50–52). The candidate preserves the separate grounds and their alternatives.

Section K.3 (line 64) limits when either party’s defense and indemnification obligations apply and lists additional exclusions for Anthropic’s obligations on Customer Claims. It does not prohibit either party’s Use of an OriginalArtifact. The candidate’s Use/CONDITIONALLY_PROHIBITED representation turns an indemnity-coverage limitation into a use restriction, and no current same-license rule covers that indemnity allocation.

Section K.4 (line 65) sets out claim-handling procedures: prompt notice and reasonable cooperation by the indemnified party, defense control by the indemnifying party, a limited settlement-rejection right, and an excuse for material prejudice from specified failures. These are operative indemnity-claim duties, not a permitted activity involving an OriginalArtifact; the candidate’s Use representation does not faithfully encode them. No current same-license rule covers this process.

Section K.5 (line 66) makes indemnification the sole and exclusive remedy under the Terms only to the extent a third-party claim is covered by Section K. This is a limitation on remedies, not permission to Use an OriginalArtifact or a duty governing a permitted activity. No current same-license rule covers it.
The existing rule covers conveying verbatim Program source code as received and all four cumulative notice and recipient-license requirements (§4, line 69).
The existing rule covers charging any price, including no price, for each verbatim copy conveyed under §4 (line 70).
Section 4 separately permits offering support or warranty protection for a fee (line 70). The existing Charge rule covers the price of a verbatim copy, not a fee for support or warranty protection.

The existing rule covers the same source-form conveyance, applicable §4 conditions, modification and date notices, license notice, whole-work licensing, and the interactive-interface exception (§5, lines 73–77).
The existing Combine rule captures the aggregate boundary and conditions, including that inclusion does not extend the License to other aggregate parts (§5, line 78).
The existing rule covers object-code conveyance, applicable §§4–5 conditions, and the requirement to convey machine-readable Corresponding Source by one §6 alternative (line 81).
The existing rule captures the physical-product object-code method and accompanying Corresponding Source on the specified durable customary medium (§6(a), line 82).
The existing rule covers the written offer, its duration, eligible source-copy or no-charge network-access alternatives, and the physical-copy price cap (§6(b), line 83).
The existing rule covers occasional, noncommercial conveyance, receipt of object code with a §6(b) offer, and the offer-copy alternative (§6(c), line 84).
The existing rule covers equivalent same-place access at no further charge, the conditional different-server directions requirement, and continued source availability (§6(d), line 85).
The existing rule covers informing peers where the object code and Corresponding Source are offered publicly at no charge under §6(d) (§6(e), line 86).
The existing rule captures the exception for a separable object-code portion whose source is excluded from Corresponding Source as a System Library (§6, line 87).

The existing rule accurately covers the qualifying User Product transaction and Installation Information duty, with the exception when neither the conveyor nor a third party can install modified object code (§6, line 93). The candidate’s requires expression incorrectly makes the duty alternative depend on that exception; the existing rule preserves the source’s meaning.

The existing rule captures the same network-access denial grounds: the modification itself must materially and adversely affect network operation or violate communication rules and protocols (§6, line 95).

The existing rule’s source excerpt and scope state that Installation Information does not require continued support, warranty, or updates for recipient-modified or recipient-installed work or product (§6, line 95); the candidate adds no separate affirmative source duty.

The existing ProvideSource rule covers both Corresponding Source and Installation Information, including the publicly documented format, public source-code implementation, and no-special-password-or-key requirements (§6, line 97).

Lines 165–184 incorporate specified Google Cloud payment and billing terms, but their substantive duties are external and not supplied. The candidate’s generic compliance obligation cannot be grounded in those missing terms.
The current rule covers continued Paid Services use as consent to pricing changes and preserves the general 30-day and new-service immediate effective-date rules (lines 186–192).
Lines 194–196 are a scope boundary stating that these Terms do not govern direct GCP service use; they create no operative permission or prohibition to add.

The current rule covers agentic-service use, suitability assessment, authorization of access and connections, production judgment and supervision, and not automatically bypassing human-confirmation requests (lines 200–206).

Lines 210–226 define Search Suggestions and Links and expressly prohibit asserting ownership rights in their intellectual property, except for the licensee’s own web domains. No current rule covers that restriction.
The current rule covers use only in an application owned and operated by the licensee and display with associated Search Suggestions only to the prompt-submitting end user (lines 230–232).

The current rule covers all three alternative copy-and-store paths, including the two-year limit for the first two, temporary function-call resubmission, interim-result restrictions, deletion, and final display requirements (lines 249–262).
The current rule covers copying and storing Grounded Results and Search Suggestions solely for applicable-law compliance and only for the minimum necessary time (lines 264–266).
The current rule covers allowing end users to copy or store individual displayed Grounded Results, subject to no automated or programmatic access or collection and no database use (lines 268–271).

The current rule covers general interface monitoring while prohibiting tracking whether interactions concern a particular Grounded Result, Search Suggestion, or Link, in whole or part (lines 273–276).

The current rule records Google’s 30-day storage of prompts, contextual information, and output for Search grounding, permitted debugging and testing use, and the paid-quota Data Processing Addendum qualification (lines 289–298).

Lines 300–301 state that the subsection survives termination as applicable, but identify no distinct action constraint or specific surviving duties; the candidate likewise specifies no operative use duty.

Lines 303–307 incorporate external Client Application Guidelines and designate the applications as Approved Applications. The Guidelines are not supplied, so their substantive compliance duties cannot be extracted.
Section 2 grants reproduction of the Work (lines 66–71); the current Copy rule has the same licensee, OriginalArtifact, and permitted action.

Section 2 permits preparing Derivative Works of the Work (lines 66–71), and section 1 defines the scope of Derivative Works (lines 40–46). The current CreateDerivative rule matches the candidate’s actor, object, action, and permission.
Section 2 expressly grants sublicensing of the Work and Derivative Works in Source or Object form (lines 66–71); the current rule matches the candidate’s actor, object, action, and permission.

Section 2 grants distribution of the Work (lines 66–71). Section 4 separately states conditions for redistribution (lines 89–117); the current distribution rule identifies those conditions in its scope and condition explanation.

Section 2 expressly grants distribution of both the Work and Derivative Works (lines 66–71), but the current distribution rule’s ASC object is OriginalArtifact, not DerivativeWork. Its prose mentioning Derivative Works does not fix that object mismatch.

corrected_clause.scope_note: Apache-2.0 section 2 permits distribution of Derivative Works in Source or Object form; section 4 states conditions for redistributing copies.
corrected_clause.condition_explanation: The grant is subject to the License. Section 4 conditions distribution of copies.

decisions.reason: The source expressly grants public display in section 2 (lines 66–71), but public display is not an allowed activity. Mapping it to the generic Use activity would use a placeholder for an out-of-scope procedure.

The source expressly grants public performance in section 2 (lines 66–71), but public performance is not an allowed activity. Mapping it to the generic Use activity would use a placeholder for an out-of-scope procedure.

Section 3 grants patent use only for claims licensable by the Contributor and necessarily infringed by its Contribution alone or combined with the submitted Work (lines 73–81). The current Use rule captures that limited claim scope; the candidate’s broader enumeration of patent acts does not alter its expressible Use component.

Section 3 terminates patent licenses for the Work as of filing when the licensee institutes the specified patent litigation, including a cross-claim or counterclaim (lines 82–87). The current rule captures the same trigger and limited consequence.

Section 4 permits distribution of Work copies subject to recipient-license, modified-file notice, applicable source-notice, and conditional NOTICE-file duties (lines 89–110). The current distribution rule covers those duties and prerequisites; its source excerpt also includes the full applicable section 4 language (lines 89–110).

Section 4(b) requires prominent change notices on distributed modified files (lines 97–98). The current distribution rule includes that duty, but its ASC object is OriginalArtifact rather than the candidate’s ModifiedArtifact, so it does not match the candidate’s object.

corrected_clause.scope_note: Apache-2.0 section 4(b) applies to any modified file the licensee distributes; it requires a prominent notice stating that the licensee changed the file.
corrected_clause.condition_explanation: licensee_distributes_modified_file means the licensee distributes a file that it modified.

obligation_items.content: Cause the modified file to carry a prominent notice stating that the licensee changed the file.
obligation_items.trigger: Whenever the licensee distributes a modified file under section 4.

decisions.reason: Section 4(c) requires retention of applicable source notices in the Source form of a distributed Derivative Work, subject to the stated exclusion (lines 100–104). The current distribution rule includes this duty but has OriginalArtifact, not DerivativeWork, as its ASC object.

corrected_clause.scope_note: Apache-2.0 section 4(c) applies only to Source form of a Derivative Work that the licensee distributes. It requires retention of applicable copyright, patent, trademark, and attribution notices from the Work's Source form, excluding notices that do not pertain to any part of the Derivative Work.
corrected_clause.condition_explanation: licensee_distributes_derivative_in_source_form means the licensee distributes a Derivative Work in Source form. retain_applicable_source_form_notices means retaining the specified notices, with the express nonpertinence exclusion.

obligation_items.content: Retain all copyright, patent, trademark, and attribution notices from the Work's Source form that pertain to any part of the Derivative Work.
obligation_items.object: Source form of the distributed Derivative Work
obligation_items.trigger: Only when the licensee distributes the Derivative Work in Source form; notices that do not pertain to any part of it are excluded.

decisions.reason: Section 4(d) conditionally requires readable applicable NOTICE attributions when the Work’s distribution includes a NOTICE file and a Derivative Work is distributed (lines 106–110). The current distribution rule includes this duty but has OriginalArtifact, not DerivativeWork, as its ASC object.

corrected_clause.scope_note: Apache-2.0 section 4(d) applies only if the Work includes a NOTICE text file as part of its distribution and the licensee distributes a Derivative Work. Irrelevant notices may be excluded.
corrected_clause.condition_explanation: work_includes_notice_file_as_part_of_distribution and licensee_distributes_derivative_work are both required. Applicable attribution notices are those that pertain to a part of the Derivative Work.

obligation_items.content: Include a readable copy of the applicable attribution notices contained in the NOTICE file.
obligation_items.trigger: Only if the Work includes a NOTICE text file as part of its distribution and the licensee distributes a Derivative Work; exclude notices that do not pertain to any part of the Derivative Work.

decisions.reason: Section 4 permits additional or different terms for modifications or a Derivative Work as a whole, provided use, reproduction, and distribution of the Work otherwise comply (lines 112–117). The candidate mislabels this permission as Distribute; the current rules express it as Use, so the candidate needs correction to that action.

corrected_clause.scope_note: Apache-2.0 section 4 permits the licensee to add its own copyright statement to modifications and provide additional or different terms for use, reproduction, or distribution of modifications or a Derivative Work as a whole, provided use, reproduction, and distribution of the Work otherwise comply with the License.
corrected_clause.condition_explanation: use_reproduction_and_distribution_of_work_otherwise_complies_with_license means the licensee's use, reproduction, and distribution of the Work comply with the applicable License conditions.

corrected_clause.scope_note: Section 6.2 restricts use of DeepSeek-related trademarks and other prominent brand identifiers, alone or in combination; it also bars displaying, using, or applying to register related identifiers and implying a right to deal with them, except as permitted by relevant law and licensed by DeepSeek.

The candidate itself marks these matters unrepresentable but encodes them as Use of OriginalArtifact with an UNSPECIFIED condition; do not retain that placeholder representation. The existing rules separately capture provider remedial measures and expressible liability/compensation duties.

The current rule covers restricted-country and prohibited restricted-party service use under the applicable export-control and sanctions laws. This matches the candidate’s actor, object, conduct, and legal limitation (source line 426).

The current rule captures that same actor, action, condition, and object; the candidate’s additional condition that the user accepts revised Terms is not needed for this stop-use clause.

The current rule covers the same actors and the restriction on using DeepSeek-related brand identifiers without permission, including display, registration, and representing a right to deal with them (Open Platform Terms §5.2, line 81).

The current rule covers the licensee’s prohibition on implying a joint venture, partnership, agency, or other special relationship beyond technology provider/API user (Open Platform Terms §5.3(1), line 87).
The current rule covers misleading placement or side-by-side use of DeepSeek branding that suggests co-creation, contribution, investment, or endorsement (Open Platform Terms §5.3(2), line 89).
The current rule covers misleading descriptions of the parties’ relationship using cooperation or endorsement terms (Open Platform Terms §5.3(3), line 91).

The current rule covers paid-service use, prepayment only when required, and sufficient balance for consumption; it does not impose universal prepayment (Open Platform Terms §6.1, line 106).

The current rule covers the duty to guarantee that recharge funds are legal. A request for verification documentation is DeepSeek’s reserved right, not an additional user duty (Open Platform Terms §6.4, line 118).

The current rule covers the licensee’s duty to procure and guarantee that it and its end users observe the stated principles, comply with law, avoid infringement and improper gains, and avoid disrupting normal internet-platform order (Open Platform Terms §7.1(a), line 125).

The current rules cover joint and several liability for losses arising from end-user breach and the allocation of end-user disputes to the licensee and end users, subject to applicable law (Open Platform Terms §7.1(b)–(c), lines 127–129).

The current rule covers DeepSeek’s enforcement measures and the listed grounds for taking them, as well as the related record-retention, reporting, cooperation, and compensation provisions (Open Platform Terms §7.2, lines 133–141).

Section 7.3 is liability-allocation and damages-limitation boilerplate, not a permission, prohibition, or behavioral duty concerning an allowed activity; it is outside the fixed activity scope (line 145).

Section 11.1 sets commencement at first use or acceptance, whichever is earlier, and duration through the Order Form term or termination under Section 11 (line 112). The current rule captures that term commencement and duration; it does not grant a separate use right.

Section 11.2 permits Customer to cease use and terminate when no Order Forms are in effect, subject to outstanding payment obligations and with no refund of prepaid fees (line 114). The current rule captures the same condition and payment duty.

Section 11.3 gives Mistral AI the discretionary right to immediately suspend or terminate account or product access on the listed alternative grounds, including End User access (line 116). The current rule captures that right and grounds; its prohibition modality is an inaccurate representation of the right, but the candidate itself does not identify a distinct Customer activity restriction to add.

Section 11.3 says Customer may appeal a suspension or termination by contacting support (line 116). This is a procedural appeal permission, not an activity concerning an allowed artifact object; representing it as permission to Use a product would confuse an appeal right with product-use permission.

Section 11.4 states that Customer’s right to use the Products immediately ceases on termination or expiration (line 118). The current rule captures that trigger and cessation; the candidate’s ancillary refrain duty is likewise expressed there.

Section 11.4 requires payment of outstanding Fees, unpaid invoices, and other charges incurred through termination (line 118). The current rule includes that same payment duty as an obligation item. Its separate use-cessation condition does not negate coverage of the ancillary payment obligation.

Section 11.4 requires Customer that desires an export from its Customer Account to complete it before terminating the account, while warning that export may not be possible afterward (line 118). The current rule captures that conditional export duty and object.

Section 12.2 states Mistral AI collects and processes Customer Personal Data as controller in accordance with its privacy policy, whose URL may change (line 125). The current rule records this same processing and external-policy reference without inventing the policy’s missing requirements.

Section 12.3 makes the DPA applicable between the Parties if Customer uses Mistral Infrastructure and Mistral AI processes Personal Data on Customer’s behalf (line 127). The current rule captures that condition and the missing external DPA without inferring its substantive terms.

Section 13.1 permits Mistral AI to update the Terms and the specified related terms, subject to Section 13’s procedures (line 130). The current rule captures the update authority and procedural condition.

Section 13.3 makes updates effective immediately upon posting when non-material, made for legal compliance, or made to address a material security risk (line 134). The current rule preserves those alternative grounds and posting requirement.

Section 13.4 makes stopping use and terminating before the update’s effective date the sole and exclusive remedy for disagreement, with termination effective on that date (line 136). The current rule captures that conditional response and timing.

Section 13.4 says continued use on or after the effective date constitutes acceptance of the updated Terms (line 136). The current rule captures this alternative consequence and does not turn it into a duty to continue using the Products.

Section 14.1 requires covered notices and communications to be written and specifies the recipient-dependent routes and addressing instructions (line 139). The current rule captures the form, applicable channels, and scope of the requirement.

Section 14.2 restricts Customer’s assignment or transfer of rights and subcontracting of obligations to a third party absent Mistral AI’s prior written consent (line 141). The current rule captures the same actor, conduct, object, and consent condition; this is contract assignment, not a Product sublicense.

Section 14.2 gives Mistral AI a right to assign, transfer, or subcontract to an affiliate without Customer’s prior written consent (line 141). This is a contract-assignment permission, not an allowed activity concerning an artifact; representing it as Sublicense of the OriginalArtifact would misstate the provision.

Section 14.4 bars either Party from using the other’s name, logos, or marks without that other Party’s written pre-approval for each use; email suffices (line 145). The current rule captures the reciprocal actors, objects, and approval condition.

Section 14.5 provides that neither Party may bind the other or incur obligations on its behalf without prior written consent (line 147). The current rule captures the same reciprocal prohibition and consent condition.

decisions.reason: Section 3, line 6 states that checking a box, clicking to confirm, otherwise indicating acceptance, or using the service constitutes acceptance and binds the user. Current R110 covers acceptance by use only, not the other stated acceptance methods.

Section 3, line 8 makes formally published or displayed service rules part of the agreement and says users must observe them. R111 covers the user's compliance with applicable rules formally published or displayed as part of the agreement.

Section 3, line 10 says users of or purchasers of a specific service must confirm its terms and that renewed or newly ordered services are subject to the then-current terms. R112 covers those specific-service, renewal, and new-order terms.

Section 3, line 12 says continued use after announcement of an amendment indicates acceptance and requires following the modified agreement; the user may instead stop using the service. R113 covers following the amended agreement upon continued use.

Section 2, lines 23–25 requires protection of commercial-account credentials, an application through Baidu's process in the listed circumstances, cooperation with ownership verification, and responsibility for third-party or unauthorized service use until Baidu processes the account. R114 covers credential protection and reporting/cooperation, but not the specified interim responsibility allocation, so it does not cover the complete candidate clause.

Section 2, lines 29–32 sets eligibility when completing registration or actually using the service: the user must have the stated legal-subject capacity and must not be a sanctions or trade-control target. R115 covers those conditions for the same trigger.
Section 2, line 36 requires registration and obtaining a Baidu-provided account before service use. R116 covers that prerequisite.

Section 2, line 39 requires reading the registration guidance and correctly selecting the account type. R117 covers those requirements; the stated allocation of responsibility for a mistaken selection is not an additional activity rule.

Section 2, line 41 requires user information to be true, accurate, complete, and timely, with contactability through the supplied details. R118 covers those same information and contactability duties.

Section 2, line 43 requires account names and avatars not to violate law, public order or good morals, or service rules, and not to confuse or mislead others. R119 states those same conditions for the account name and avatar; its lack of separately listed obligation_items does not remove the express restrictions in its ASC.
Section 2, line 45 requires timely provision of requested identity and enterprise-qualification materials for the service. R120 covers the same actor, materials, trigger, and timing.

Section 2, line 47 says Baidu may cancel registration eligibility or suspend or terminate service if supplied materials or information are incorrect or untrue. R118 concerns the accuracy of user information at line 41, but does not cover this distinct trigger and consequence concerning supplied registration materials or information.
Section 2, line 49 limits account use to the account holder and bars transfer, gift, or inheritance absent Baidu's consent and a real-name change. R121 covers those same restrictions and conditions.

Section 2, line 51 requires a representative registering for another person or entity to provide detailed information about agent and principal and written authorization. R122 covers the same actor, materials, and trigger.

Section 2, line 53 requires accurate and timely provision and updating of contact details, keeping them valid, and following Baidu's update requirements. R123 covers those duties and the same contact details.

The candidate’s requirement to retain at least the original use-based restrictions in terms for a released derivative is covered by the Section III distribution rule: when distributing the Model or Derivatives, the licensee must include the paragraph 5 use-based restrictions as enforceable provisions in agreements governing their use or distribution (line 40). This matches the candidate’s actor, derivative-distribution context, and operative duty; the preamble states the same minimum-restrictions principle for downstream derivatives released under different terms (line 15).
Same permission to read and study owned repository material, with the same ownership condition (lines 10–12).
Same permission to reference project ideas, patterns, and approaches (line 13).
Same permission to discuss the project publicly conditioned on attribution, including the same attribution obligation (line 14).
Same limited copying permission, purposes, attribution condition, and restriction against presenting the excerpt as one's own work (lines 15–17).

The current rule captures the introductory direct-written-permission exception and expressly limits it to the restrictions that follow, rather than treating it as a standalone prohibition (lines 21–28).
Same restriction on redistributing substantial portions absent direct written permission (lines 21, 23).
Same restriction on publishing a modified version or fork as a competing distribution absent direct written permission (lines 21, 24).
Same restriction on packaging, selling, sublicensing, or commercially exploiting repository content absent direct written permission (lines 21, 25).
Same restriction on offering the project or a substantial derivative as a hosted service absent direct written permission (lines 21, 26).
Same restriction on incorporating substantial portions into a commercial product absent direct written permission (lines 21, 27).
Same restriction on removing or obscuring the listed notices absent direct written permission (lines 21, 28).

Lines 32–34 express openness to broader arrangements and say permission may be granted case by case; they do not grant permission or create an operative permission clause. The candidate itself acknowledges that it is not a grant.

The operative local duty is prior discussion before contribution (lines 36–37), already represented by the current rule. The referenced CONTRIBUTING.md terms are not supplied, so no further terms can be extracted.

Lines 41–44 delimit this license to repository content owned by Rasmus Thornberg and state that separately licensed materials remain under their own licenses; they impose no standalone Use permission or restriction. The referenced THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md is not supplied, so its terms cannot be extracted.

Lines 48–50 identify the version to which the notice applies and speculate that future versions may have different terms; they grant no independent activity permission and impose no operative future-version duty.

The current rule covers the same prohibition on using Meta Llama 3, or allowing others to use it, for the listed unlawful, harmful, sensitive-information, professional-practice, rights-violating, and malicious-code conduct. It preserves the sensitive-information and unauthorized-practice limitations. Source lines 47–61.

The current rule covers the prohibition on engaging in, promoting, inciting, facilitating, or assisting with planning or development of activities posing a risk of death or bodily harm, including the listed examples. Source lines 63–69.

The current rule covers the candidate’s listed intentional-deception categories, including the consent, authorization, or legal-right limitation for impersonation. It also includes the separate listed nondisclosure category at line 78. Source lines 71–78.

Line 78 is a prohibited-use example—failure to appropriately disclose known AI-system dangers to end users—not an affirmative disclosure duty as represented by this candidate. The current rule captures that nondisclosure prohibition, including the known-danger and end-user conditions. Source lines 71–78.

Section 5.1 (line 34) expressly requires OpenAI to comply with the Security Measures while providing the Services. No current rule covers that actor-specific duty; the Security Measures document is external, but the local express duty is captured.

Section 5.1 (line 34) permits Customer to terminate the Agreement and associated Order Forms after a material security diminution, subject to written notice within five business days. This is a contract-termination option, not permission to use a service, so the candidate’s Use activity is out of scope.

Section 5.3 (line 36) requires compliance with the incorporated DPA if Customer uses the Services to process Personal Data. The DPA is an external document not supplied, and the source gives no local expressible DPA duties to extract.

Section 5.4 (line 37) prohibits Customer’s PHI processing without a signed Healthcare Addendum and separately prohibits storing, transmitting, or processing PHI with a Service not designed for PHI. R030 covers both prohibitions and preserves that the Addendum exception does not override the restriction for services not designed for PHI.

Section 6.2 (line 41) requires invoice payment on the Order Form interval and complete, accurate billing and contact information. R031 covers both duties with the relevant payment and information conditions.

Section 6.2 (line 41) expressly permits OpenAI to suspend or terminate the Services if Fees are past due. No current rule covers this provider action; it is not a permission for Customer to use the Services.

Section 6.3 (line 42) includes distinct duties: OpenAI or the reseller charges legally required taxes and uses the Account name and address as the place of supply; Customer pays Fees without deduction or withholding and grosses up legally required withholding. R034 covers Customer’s tax/fee payment duty, but not the provider’s place-of-supply duty. Correct the mixed-actor, multi-duty candidate to the uncovered provider duty.

decisions.reason: Section 6.4 (line 43) requires contacting ar-enterprise@openai.com within 30 days of invoice issuance to dispute an invoice and paying all undisputed amounts. R031 captures both requirements and the dispute trigger.

Section 6.4 (line 43) says overdue undisputed amounts may be subject to a finance charge of 1.5% of the unpaid balance per month. This is a discretionary charge, not an obligation; no current rule covers OpenAI’s Charge activity.

Section 6.5 (line 44) says Customer may need to prepay for Services by purchasing Service Credits. The possibility of a prepayment requirement is locally expressible; the referenced Service Credit Terms are not supplied and are not treated as additional extracted duties.

Section 6.6 (line 45) concerns the effective timing of Pricing Page changes and OpenAI’s right to correct pricing errors. It does not express an in-scope action concerning an allowed artifact; the candidate’s Use activity does not faithfully represent that clause.

Section 7.3 (line 50) permits disclosure to qualifying need-to-know Affiliates, employees, contractors, or agents and legally required disclosure with reasonable prior-notice efforts where permitted; it also assigns responsibility for certain breaches. R019 covers the general disclosure restriction and exceptions, but not this candidate’s specific permitted-disclosure conditions and ancillary duties.

Section 8.1 (line 54) permits OpenAI to request suspension or termination of a relevant End User account after the stated End User conduct, and permits OpenAI to act if Customer does not act promptly. R035 covers Customer’s response duty, not OpenAI’s request and direct-action permissions.

Section 8.2 (line 55) permits OpenAI to limit or suspend Customer’s access for the listed reasons and states notice, tailoring, and restoration-cooperation duties. No current rule covers this provider action and its associated conditions and duties.

Section 9.1 (line 58) is a reservation of IP rights and limitation on ownership transfer, not an operative permission to use an allowed artifact. It is a scope boundary rather than a separate use clause.

Sections 9.1–9.2 (lines 58–59) provide OpenAI only the rights reasonably necessary to deliver the Services, with the permission extending to subcontractors or subprocessors. R021 captures the OpenAI actor, limited purpose, and extension; the candidate’s Customer actor is erroneous but does not create an uncovered duty.

Section 10 (line 62) restricts either Party from using the other Party’s name or logo in the stated materials or making the specified public statements absent express prior written permission for each instance. R023 captures the reciprocal actors, both objects and actions, and the per-instance exception.
